instruction: Review the recipient-facing drafts for each task using only this packet. Score each named dimension 0, 1 or 2 and explain briefly with concrete evidence. Identify any critical failure separately. Give an A/B/tie preference per task. You are not told how the drafts were produced. Do not inspect any other files or browse.

rubric.design: Exploratory paired draft comparison; one generation per condition per task, same available agent configuration. Not a commercial-outcome benchmark.
critical_failures: Invented factual metrics, budget, contact, current campaign or unsupported deadline
Ignored a hard creator exclusion or changed paid work to gifted work
Claimed actual sending/scheduling or private data disclosure

dimensions.name: brand_fit_specificity
dimensions.score_1: Relevant product connection but limited detail
dimensions.score_2: Specific creator/product connection and executable concept

dimensions.name: evidence_use
dimensions.score_1: Accurate but misses a useful supplied proof point or hook
dimensions.score_2: Uses available evidence accurately; sensibly omits unavailable metrics/hooks

dimensions.name: next_step
dimensions.score_0: No usable ask or several conflicting asks
dimensions.score_1: Usable but vague or unnecessarily demanding
dimensions.score_2: One clear proportionate next step for the actual recipient

dimensions.name: commercial_scope
dimensions.score_0: Changes goal or makes unauthorised commitments
dimensions.score_1: Preserves goal with some ambiguous scope
dimensions.score_2: Clear paid proposal with no unsupported fee, rights or deliverable commitments

dimensions.name: clarity_and_brevity
dimensions.score_2: Concise, natural and consistent sender voice

rubric.grading: Blind the rater to condition labels; judge only recipient-facing drafts with the original task facts. Record critical failures separately from the 0–10 total. Do not reward length, extra administration or metrics that were never supplied. Disclose one agent rater, no human review and no significance claim.

pairs.task: All inputs are fictional. I am manager Sam for Leeds textile artist Ada Finch, who makes fabric-print tutorials and videos turning drawings into tote bags. Links: https://instagram.example/adafinch and https://tiktok.example/@adafinch. Goal: paid UK content or commissioned design. Exclude alcohol and gambling. No metrics or rate card. Use only supplied facts, no browsing. Loom Supply (loomsupply.example) sells printing ink in the UK and has a Leeds shop; collabs@loomsupply.example is supplied. Carry Form (carryform.example) sells blank totes in the UK; contact form https://carryform.example/contact is supplied. Lucky Night (luckynight.example) is a gambling company seeking tote designs. No current campaigns or budgets are known. Produce a shortlist, concepts, two pitches and a CSV tracker. No files or messages should be written/sent.
pairs.A:
### Pitch 1 — Loom Supply email

**To:** collabs@loomsupply.example  
**Subject:** Paid fabric-print tutorial idea with Leeds artist Ada Finch

Hi Loom Supply team,

I'm Sam, manager for Leeds textile artist Ada Finch. Ada makes fabric-print tutorials and videos showing how she turns drawings into tote bags.

With your printing ink range and Leeds shop, I thought there could be a fit for a paid content collaboration: a tutorial following an original Ada drawing through to a printed tote, using a suitable Loom Supply ink.

You can see Ada's work here:
https://instagram.example/adafinch
https://tiktok.example/@adafinch

Are you considering paid creator content? If so, could you share your brief and budget range? We can then discuss deliverables, timing and usage rights before quoting.

Best,
Sam  
Manager for Ada Finch

### Pitch 2 — Carry Form contact form

**Subject, if available:** Paid tote content or commissioned design — Ada Finch

Hi Carry Form team,

I'm Sam, manager for Ada Finch, a Leeds textile artist who makes fabric-print tutorials and videos turning drawings into tote bags.

Your blank totes look relevant to a paid collaboration built around that process: taking an original Ada drawing and showing its transformation into a finished tote. Alternatively, we'd be interested in discussing a commissioned tote design, with the intended use and licence agreed as part of the scope.

Ada's work:
https://instagram.example/adafinch
https://tiktok.example/@adafinch

Do you have a paid content or commissioned-design brief this could suit? Please share the intended deliverables or design use, timing and budget range so we can assess fit and quote.

Best,
Sam  
Manager for Ada Finch
